one_liner: A wide-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 1.2x fair value. Interesting below about $368.

profile.what: Meta owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, used by more than three billion people a day. It is spending heavily on AI models and data centres and on Reality Labs (virtual-reality headsets and smart glasses).
profile.money: Almost entirely advertising: about 98% of 2025 revenue. Businesses buy ads targeted by Meta's AI ranking systems. Revenue grows with the number of ads shown and the price per ad. Reality Labs loses more than $15 billion a year.
profile.valued: Meta is valued on P/E and free cash flow, and the debate is about its spending: the market rewards it when ad growth outruns AI capital expenditure and punishes it when spending runs ahead of returns.

summary.sentence: A hugely profitable advertising business funding one of the largest AI spending programmes anywhere.
strengths: Billions of users across several apps.
risks: Capital spending has consumed most of operating cash flow.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow, capex held at depreciation: $68.0B a year: operating cash flow less depreciation and stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). Capex is running at 4.2x depreciation, so most of it is expansion, not upkeep. (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 7–13% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 38%; cost of capital 9.3%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
